newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INCE, KAREMBEU, BIERHOFF GET TWO MATCH BANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INCE, KAREMBEU, BIERHOFF GET TWO MATCH BANS.

text.p: England midfielder Paul Ince, French international Christian Karembeu and Germany's Euro 96 star forward Oliver Bierhoff were given two match bans by Italy's Serie A sporting judge on Wednesday.
The ban for Inter's Ince was the most controversial, following his sending off at the weekend in the Milan club's 2-0 home victory over Piacenza.

Ince was shown the red card after Piacenza's Giampietro Piovani, waiting for a corner to be taken, collapsed theatrically in the goalmouth clutching his head as if he had been hit by the Englishman in an off the ball foul.

Television replays showed clearly that Ince had merely tweaked the Italian's ear. Ince, who is black, appeared to have been provoked also by a racist taunt that Piovani later admitted making in the heat of the moment.
Piovani, who was sent off in the closing seconds for elbowing an opponent, was also banned for two matches.
Sampdoria's Karembeu was sent off in the second half of his team's 2-1 defeat against Bologna on Sunday for hitting opponent Igor Shalimov after being fouled by the Russian.
Bierhoff was sent off for a particularly bad foul in Udinese's 1-1 draw at Napoli on Sunday. The German had earlier scored his team's equaliser.
